title: I vibecoded and released Football Heritage — a free browser football manager with deep tactics, 2D matches, and long personalizable careers.
author: Xolfyy
selftext:
Hey everyone!

I made **Football Heritage**, a completely free football management game built with the help of AI.

The idea behind it was fairly simple: I wanted something that sits between the incredibly detailed, spreadsheet-heavy football management simulators and the much more casual alternatives.

I love the depth of proper football management games, but I also think there's room for something that doesn't require hours of learning menus just to enjoy a season. At the same time, I didn't want a game where you simply buy a few players, press simulate, and hope for the best.

I wanted the decisions to matter. Building a squad, understanding your opponents, finding the right tactics, developing young players, managing finances, and gradually creating your own football history.

Something you could open on your phone for ten minutes or spend an entire evening playing on your PC.

**Football Heritage is the result, and it's available to play for free.**

[https://playfootballheritage.com/](https://playfootballheritage.com/)

# Workflow

Football Heritage was built primarily using **GPT-5.6 and GPT-6.1 High**.

The workflow was based on continuous iteration.

The foundation was the football simulation itself: generating a football world, creating clubs and players, running leagues, calculating match results, and keeping everything connected across seasons.

From there, I gradually expanded the systems. Transfers, scouting, contracts, youth development, finances, facilities, sponsorships, continental competitions, manager careers, and increasingly detailed tactical mechanics.

As more features were introduced, existing systems needed adjustments and fixes of their own. A new mechanic couldn't simply exist in isolation; it had to work with the rest of the simulation.

The interface also went through a substantial redesign. I wanted something cleaner and more approachable than the traditional dense management-game layout, while still keeping the information and controls easily accessible. That eventually led to a responsive interface designed for both desktop and mobile, with light and dark modes.

One of the biggest additions was the **2D live match engine**. The game already supported instant results and text-based match simulations, but I wanted players to have the option of actually watching matches unfold on a pitch. That meant adding player movement, match events, playback controls, statistical views, and the systems needed to connect that presentation with the underlying simulation.

Other development stages focused on expanding career customization, improving the save and backup system, adding translations, building achievements, introducing additional game modes, and resolving bugs and inconsistencies throughout the project.

The result is a surprisingly extensive, interconnected browser game built through an iterative AI coding workflow.

And most importantly, **it's a finished, released game that anyone can play right now.**

# What exactly is Football Heritage?

In Football Heritage you take charge of a club and make the decisions that shape its future. You might begin with a smaller team, work your way up through the divisions, develop a generation of young players, or eventually take over a completely different club.

Your career isn't limited to a single team or a single season. The world continues developing around you, with leagues, transfers, competitions, and managerial opportunities creating new challenges over time.

The goal was to give players plenty of control without turning every part of the experience into unnecessary work.

# Build the football world you want

One of the things I particularly like is how much freedom you have before your career even begins.

You can choose between **men's and women's football**, select a starting season anywhere from **1980/81 to 2040/41**, and decide which countries, leagues, and divisions should be included in your world.

Want to start a career decades in the past and build your own version of football history? You can.

Prefer beginning in the present day with a smaller football world? That works too.

There is a **Quick Start** option for jumping straight into the game, but also a much more detailed custom career setup where you can adjust difficulty, financial conditions, transfer inflation, injuries, fitness, match randomness, and other simulation rules.

There are even optional cheats if you want to experiment with different scenarios or simply enjoy a less restrictive career.

# Tactics that actually influence your chances

This is probably one of my favourite aspects of the game.

You can build your starting XI, change formations, manage substitutions, and adjust **20 tactical controls** affecting how your team plays.

You can study your next opponent, examine their strengths, and see your team's estimated probabilities of winning, drawing, or losing.

Those probabilities take your squad, tactical choices, fitness, preparation, and other factors into account.

For example, you might initially have a 65% chance of winning. By finding a better tactical approach against that particular opponent, you could improve those odds.

Nothing guarantees a victory, of course. But it makes tactical preparation feel worthwhile rather than decorative.

I wanted players to feel like they're actually managing a football team, not simply watching random results appear.

# Three ways to experience matches

Not everyone wants to spend the same amount of time on matchday, so the game offers three different options:

* **Quick Sim:** Simulate the result immediately and continue with your season.
* **Classic Live Simulation:** Follow the match through live text commentary, events, and statistics.
* **2D Live Simulation:** Watch players move around the pitch as the match unfolds, with playback controls, match events, and detailed statistical information.

The 2D mode also lets you follow individual player situations, possession, xG, and other match information.

You can quickly simulate less important fixtures or take your time watching a cup final or a match that could decide your entire season.

# There's much more to manage than matchday

The management side includes quite a few interconnected systems.

You can buy and sell players, negotiate contracts, arrange loans, sign free agents, manage wages, and search the transfer market for players who fit your plans.

Scouting and youth development are also important. You can search different regions for talent, invest in your academy, and try to turn promising youngsters into the future of your club.

You also have responsibility for the club beyond the squad.

There are **upgradeable facilities**, including training facilities, the youth academy, recruitment network, rehabilitation centre, and stadium. You can invest in commercial development too, including merchandise operations and the club's social media department.

Sponsorships, commercial partnerships, club finances, and long-term investments all play a part in how your team develops.

The football world includes multiple divisions, promotion and relegation, domestic cups, and continental competitions such as the **Champions Crown, Continental Shield, and Founders Cup**.

There's a calendar for keeping track of fixtures and important dates, alongside records of your seasons, results, transfers, trophies, and managerial career.

And your story doesn't have to end at the club where it began. As your reputation develops, you can pursue opportunities elsewhere and continue your career with another team.

# Some extra features I wanted to include

Beyond the traditional football management mechanics, Football Heritage has a few additional systems.

There's an **achievement and challenge system**, including some difficult long-term objectives for players who enjoy building careers across many seasons.

You can also generate downloadable graphics from your save, including player cards, financial summaries, and managerial career images.

The game includes two optional special modes called **Thunder and Blitz**, currently marked as beta features. They introduce rhythm and reaction-based challenges alongside the standard management experience, for anyone who wants to try something a little different.

The interface supports **15 languages**, and you can switch between light and dark themes.

# Completely free, with local saves and no account required

I wanted Football Heritage to be as accessible as possible.

**There are no subscriptions, purchases, paid features, or accounts required.** You simply open the website and play.

The game works directly in your browser on **phones, tablets, laptops, and desktop PCs**, with layouts adapted to different screen sizes.

Your careers are saved locally on your device. You can also export them as backup files and import them again whenever you want.

This means you can move a career between devices manually without needing an online account or cloud synchronization.

You can play a few matches during a short break, return to your save later, or spend hours working through a long managerial career.

# A final word

I'm not trying to present Football Heritage as a replacement for the biggest football management simulators. Those games have enormous teams, resources, and levels of detail behind them.

What I wanted to build was something different.

A game that captures the satisfaction of football management without making it feel like a chore to learn. Something where discovering a great young player, preparing the perfect tactic, winning promotion, or finally lifting a continental trophy can be genuinely rewarding.

But also something you can simply open in your browser and enjoy.

**Football Heritage is completely free and available to play now:**

[https://playfootballheritage.com/](https://playfootballheritage.com/)

I'd genuinely love to hear what you think, especially from people who enjoy football management games.

And if you end up enjoying it, I'd really appreciate you sharing it with a friend or anyone who might be interested. The game is still reaching a fairly small audience, so even a recommendation would mean a lot and help more people discover it.

Thanks for taking the time to check it out!

**Your club. Your story. Your heritage.**

comments.body: Why would anyone play this over FM?

replies.author: Xolfyy
replies.body: There are players who would like to get into football simulator games, but find FM too complex, and don't want to learn the game, and fine the alternavies to be lacking and way too simplistic. They are the main audience. Also, there are many features and options in this game which are pretty unique to it, someone can like those as well.

replies.author: Xolfyy
replies.body: The main point of this game is not realism or the simulation experience. It's similar to a situation where some people want to play a World War II game but don't want to learn how to play HOI 4
